the use of conventional sodium channel blockers in multiple sclerosis is limited by their side effects, but that a novel central nervous systems excluded sodium channel blocker that is selectively targeted to lesions during the inflammatory phase of multiple sclerosis may be useful in the treatment of progressive neurodegeneration and disability in multiple sclerosis.

the therapeutic targeting of neuroprotection during periods of the penumbra in multiple sclerosis lesions may improve the potential therapeutic index and limit the development of chronic neurodegeneration in this disease.
